sc: Well 3-year-old, cold 2 weeks ago, sudden petechiae, platelets 15, Hb and WBC normal → ITP: observe if only skin bleeding
Boy, bleeding after circumcision, swollen knee after a fall, long APTT → Haemophilia: factor VIII/IX assay
Teenage girl with heavy periods and nosebleeds, mother the same → Von Willebrand disease
f: Petechiae, gums, nose = platelets · joints and muscles = clotting factors
CBC + film, PT, APTT · long APTT alone: haemophilia · long PT + APTT: vitamin K, liver, DIC · low platelets: ITP, leukaemia, DIC
Post-viral, well child, isolated low platelets · 80% recover · skin only: observe · mucosal bleeding: prednisolone 2–4 mg/kg 5–7 days or IVIG 0.8–1 g/kg
X-linked, boys · A: factor VIII, B: IX · severe < 1% · replace factor (joint 40–60%, head 80–100%) · mild A: desmopressin
vWD: long bleeding time, desmopressin · DIC: septic, low fibrinogen · HSP: purpura with normal platelets · Wiskott–Aldrich: eczema, small platelets
Spontaneous bleeding when platelets < 20 × 10⁹/L · chronic ITP > 12 months
trap: Low platelets with big spleen, pallor, nodes or bone pain is not ITP: bone marrow first · head injury in haemophilia: factor first, then CT · always ask if the bruises fit the story
